title_page_text: You are invited to submit a quotation for Provision of a West Midlands Creative Business ‘Scale-Up’ Ready Mapping Study to Greater Birmingham and Solihull Local Enterprise Partnership (GBSLEP), no later than noon on Tuesday 30th July 2019 as detailed below in accordance with GBSLEP's standard terms and conditions of contract:

Quotation providers are advised to ensure that they are fully familiar with the nature and extent of the contract. It is the responsibility of the Quotation provider to obtain for themselves, at their own expense, all information necessary for the preparation of their quotation.
Quotations must be submitted for the entire service as detailed below; quotations for only part of the service may be rejected.
GBSLEP may at its own absolute discretion extend the closing date and time specified for the receipt of quotations or invite variations to the terms of the contract.
GBSLEP will evaluate this Quotation based on criteria of 70% Quality and 30% Price as described in paragraph 4.1.
GBSLEP does not bind itself to accept the lowest or any quotation and reserves the right to accept a quotation either in whole or part for the goods and services specified.
All prices shall in all cases be exclusive of VAT, which will be applied in accordance with legislation. Discounts, trade allowances of any kind must be shown separately.

If a Bidder is in doubt as to the interpretation of any part of this document; or if they consider that any of its requirements are ambiguous or conflict with any other requirements, they should contact GBSLEP via fiona.Latter@wmca.org.uk or procurement@gbslep.co.uk and we will endeavour to answer enquiries prior to quotations being submitted. The answer may be circulated to other Bidders, where appropriate. This clarification phase is available between 8 July 2019 to 24th July 2019. Note that clarifications outside of these timescales will not be considered.
The Bidder should submit their completed bid to both fiona.latter@wmca.org.uk and procurement@gbslep.co.uk by the required deadline.
GBSLEP requires a supplier for the provision of a Creative Business Mapping Study.

This contract will cover a period of up to 12 months between 1st Aug 2019 to 31st July 2020. It is envisaged, however, that most of the work will be completed before Christmas 2019. The contract may be renewed.

title_page_text: This is a two phase process, initially identifying all DCI companies followed by a detailed interrogation to identify those with scale up potential.
We try to the make the process as linear as possible but have left time in each work package for iterative refinement against key data sources.
This process will result in a tiered list of companies who score (red, amber, green) against scale up gateway criteria and confidence factors. (see table for examples).
Phase. 1 – Identification of DCI companies for further investigation

This process is made up of 4 steps that will enable us to gather a broad list of Creative and Digital companies within WMCA. Phase 2 will take this list and define their growth potential and identify their contact details.
Phase 1 will also create a directory of all Creative and Digital companies within WMCA. NOTE FOR IAIN – WE NEED TO BE CLEAR THAT THIS WON’T AND SHOULDN’T INCLUDE EMAIL CONTACT DETAILS.
Phase. 2 – Analysis of broad list to identify high growth companies

This process is made up of 5 steps that will enable us to analyse the companies gathered in phase 1 and create a detailed list of high growth creative and digital scaleup candidate companies within the WMCA.
This will include a score for each high growth category:
Financial growth – actual based upon accounts from previous 3 years to identify growth of at least 10%
Employees – number of employees and contractors to identify at least 8 employees
Private sector investment – volume of investment and potential IP
Public investment – grants received and potential IP

title_page_text: Further to our recent conversations, I’m attaching a summary note for you to share with colleagues at WMCA, Greater Manchester and West of England. As we discussed, this summarises our proprietary methodology and is to help you determine how to tender the mapping work you need. I am comfortable that, as discussed, you have no intention to include this within the invitation to tender or specification for any work required; but thought it would be helpful for you to see the level of detail that our method returns.

Our approach combines a mixture of secondary data sources, including a web search that, if carried out at scale, is best conducted in two stages: an initial ‘scraping’ of web sites using artificial intelligence, followed by a manual process of assurance. The cost of any mapping is determined by your specification, eg: which geographies? How many qualified company records do you require? Do you need us to provide contact details for each of those companies? Do you want to include a survey of a sample of those businesses to test both the findings from the mix of secondary sources and the marketing messages you want to put out to creative enterprises?
We start from multiple sources of data, eg:

Existing company records held by the client and partner organisations  and contacts from other business support, sector development and scale up programmes (both of which help to ‘train’ the AI web search)
